name: MMX
first: First sample return from a Martian moon
description: Martian Moons eXploration is JAXA's plan to land on Phobos, scoop ~10 g of regolith, and bring it home. The samples may settle a long-debated question: are Phobos and Deimos captured asteroids, or fragments from an ancient impact on Mars itself? The mission also includes a German-French rover for Phobos surface mobility — a wholly different operations model from anything the Hayabusa missions did at Itokawa or Ryugu. Launch slipped from 2024 to 2026 with the delays of JAXA's H3 rocket; MMX lifted off on 19 October 2026 and is due to enter Mars orbit in August 2027.

events.label: LAUNCH
events.note: H3 flight 10 from Tanegashima, 19 October 2026 — the first H3 to send a spacecraft to another planet.

events.label: MARS ORBIT INSERTION
events.note: Capture into Mars orbit; transfer to Phobos quasi-orbit over following months.

events.label: ROVER DEPLOY
events.note: DLR/CNES rover (~25 kg) released onto Phobos surface for in-situ studies.

events.label: PHOBOS SAMPLE
events.note: MMX touches down on Phobos; ~10 g of regolith collected.

events.label: EARTH RETURN
events.note: Sample re-entry capsule arrives at Earth ~2031.
